claims.text: Integrated data-driven optimization can precisely tune magnetic interactions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy thin films.
Tuning magnetic interactions through data-driven optimization enhances the magnetocaloric effect near magnetic phase-transition temperatures.
Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy thin films have complex microstructures.
Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy thin films possess intrinsic interfacial stresses.
The proposed optimization method couples high-resolution magnetization measurements with computational simulations of thin-film processing and microstructure evolution.
Processing conditions selected by the data-driven model tailor microstructural features.
Processing conditions selected by the data-driven model tailor interfacial characteristics.
Machine-learning algorithms can correlate processing parameters with microstructural evolution in non-equiatomic HEA thin films.
Machine-learning algorithms can correlate processing parameters with magnetic behavior in non-equiatomic HEA thin films.
Correlations learned from processing, microstructure, and magnetic data permit fine control of magnetic interactions.
Magnetic interactions govern the magnetocaloric response.
Data-driven optimization will produce a measurable shift in magnetic phase-transition temperatures relative to conventional processing.
Data-driven optimization will enhance the magnetocaloric effect, including increased magnetic entropy change, relative to conventional processing.
The proposed tuning method is expected to be effective specifically in low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
The method's performance may differ in bulk samples or equiatomic alloys.
